title: Scope a retired-terms registry entry to the cyberfleet sense of seat/bunker/desk
what: This CR retires seat, seated, seating, bunker, and desk within the cyberfleet Operator node, while all three words stay live and correct in sibling scopes. The retired-terms registry supports scope plus allow, so an entry scoped to this node would guard the rename without false-firing on the legitimate homonyms. Deliberately not filed during the spec phase: the implementation still carried the retired terms until deliver landed, so an entry added then would have failed closed against the repo's own tree.

title: Decide whether the doctrine-altitude Bunker needs disambiguating from the retired cyberfleet sense
what: Bunker names two different things in this corpus. The cyberfleet sense (Operator's place) is retired by this CR. The SDD sense (the fleet-level command altitude where the Scanner sits) is untouched and still correct. They no longer collide in practice, but nothing records that they are different referents, so a future sweep could rename the wrong one. Held out of scope as a different project's vocabulary.

title: Decide whether the attended-vs-headless seat should be renamed too
what: The cyberlegion plugin uses seat in an unrelated sense — whether a live user channel exists, as in do I have a seat, which forces run-inline. That sense is untouched here and remains valid. Now that the fleet sense is retired, the word survives in the corpus meaning only this, which is either a clarification or a trap depending on whether a reader knows both histories. Worth its own de-dup decision.

title: Remove the non-discriminating rubric scenario from the operator suite
what: Two independent cold judge rounds confirmed the pre-existing rubric scenario cannot fail: all four dimensions re-grade properties boolean scenarios in the same suite already decide, two are double-barreled which fails rubric structure before any scoring, and every dimension's terms are lifted from the node README so a config-quoting run banks at or near max against a threshold of seven of nine. The remedy is deletion rather than repair, since all four properties are already decided as booleans. Deferred by owner decision to keep this CR single-purpose; deleting a scenario is a real coverage reduction, a different edit class from a rename, and deserves its own gate.

title: Bridge the governing ADR's retired vocabulary to the current terms
what: The node README cites the governing ADR's amendment item for the anti-probe rule, and that item still uses the retired noun. The ADR is an append-only historical record and is correctly unmodified, but a reader following the citation meets vocabulary the node no longer uses, with nothing marking the two as the same rule. A short amendment note pointing at the current terms would close the seam.

title: Scope the voice bar's status-acknowledgment carve-out to a named class
what: The shipped skill resolves a genuine ambiguity — a clipped acknowledgment is status, not padding — but phrases the carve-out as an open class, saying status is always in bounds. The impl-judge found it does not currently license role-play, because the immediately following unconditional never-role-play-a-human paragraph still disciplines any output, and passed the scenario. The residual risk is that an open class invites more than it names. Naming the class specifically, for example readiness acknowledgments, would close it. Deliberately not fixed after the verdict: the carve-out lives in the judged subject, so editing it post-verdict would mean the verdict no longer rests on the shipped text.

why: Implementation matches the frozen suite. Mechanism drift independently refuted by a normalized multiset diff of every command span HEAD vs working tree. Both known recurrence sites clean. First gate attempt failed on child-to-parent transport, not judgment; its 15 blind runs are corroborating evidence in this shard and were never relayed into a verdict.

title: ACED impl-judge cannot collect its own case-judge results
what: The ACED impl-judge fans out one case-judge per scenario and awaits their verdicts. In this session all 15 children completed their two-pass protocol correctly but none could address the parent — SendMessage reported no reachable agent by the parent's name, and the children had no agent-listing tool to resolve a real address, so every verdict surfaced to the conductor instead. The judge cannot complete and correctly returns undetermined rather than fabricate. This blocks a completion claim the mission made: the ACED squad is the registry-resolved impl-judge for artifact-type skill, so any CR judged by it in this configuration cannot reach a verdict through its own harness. This CR reached its gate only by substituting an inline judge that does not fan out. Classified blocking because it contradicts the claim that the resolved production chain is runnable end to end.

why: Retracted before merge on the owner's call after evaluation. It was the only behavior change in a vocabulary CR and required an explicit carve-out from the Clearance in every record that described it. It took two attempts and produced two defects, neither caught by design: the first banned a conforming terse acknowledgment, and the fix for that introduced an open-class carve-out still open at the time of retraction. The bar itself was inferred from a one-line instruction and never affirmatively specified, yet would have graded every future run. It was also the softest-verified change in the CR — the rename carries mechanical proof, a voice bar carries simulation. Deferred to its own CR where the bar can be specified and calibrated in both directions.
fidelity: Restoration verified exact: the @quality scenario differs from pre-CR by one word, the retired place-noun dropped from its title, with all three Then clauses byte-identical; the shipped SKILL.md Output section is whitespace-normalized identical to pre-CR. Scenario count unchanged at 41. No re-judgment required — contract and implementation are both back to the previously implemented and passing state.

title: Specify the Operator voice bar as an AI agent rather than a performed character
what: Retracted from the vocabulary CR and owed its own change. The intent stands: Operator is an AI agent operating the fleet and should read as one rather than perform a human character. Doing it properly needs the bar specified rather than inferred — what counts as role-play, what the named carve-out class for status acknowledgments is, and calibration in both directions so it kills a performing run while leaving a conforming terse run passing. The first attempt failed both directions in turn, so both matter. Supersedes the earlier follow-up about scoping the carve-out's open class, which only existed to defend the retracted clause.

result: ALIGNED true on all three lenses, no blocking finding
why: Re-run after the voice-bar retraction to confirm the final state. Retraction verified clean by the judge's own extraction against the pre-CR revision, not from the conductor's diff: the @quality scenario's Given, When and all three Then clauses byte-identical to pre-CR with the sole delta being the retired place-noun dropped from the title; zero retired terms anywhere in the node, so the rename was not collaterally damaged; zero voice-bar prose anywhere in the node, so no orphan. 41 scenarios and 130 step lines in and out; all 12 cyberlegion command strings multiset-identical.

Re-run after the voice-bar retraction. SKILL.md's Output section verified whitespace-normalized identical to pre-CR; the retraction commit's diff isolated and confirmed to touch only voice-bar lines, never rename lines. Token-multiset command diff against main surfaced exactly one addition, `cyberlegion unit close <id>`, which the judge traced to an earlier commit on this branch rather than assuming it was drift. Absorption read over all 41 Givens found no trigger-example apparatus in the implementation.

what: The ratified spec-gate why still carried diff figures true only while the voice tightening was in: `9 of the 13 reworded scenarios` in the confidence block, and `all 13 reworded scenario titles` in the floor block. The spec-judge flagged the first; the conductor independently recounted (11 reworded titles, 7 with byte-identical Then blocks, 4 changed by one noun), confirmed the judge's figures, then swept and found the second instance the judge had not named. Both now carry before-and-after figures so a reader checking the final diff against the record finds no discrepancy. Rule: a gate why is the durable justification a later reader relies on, so it must describe the diff that actually landed, not an intermediate state.

The impl-judge noted that spec.md's impl-approval note contains prose describing a prior cold-judge verdict, and explicitly declined to treat it as evidence, resting every cell on its own reading instead. Recorded because it identifies a contamination vector: a gate why that narrates a judge's findings is readable by any future cold judge of the same node. The discipline held here; the seam is worth knowing about.
